official_measurement_examples.name: Green Belt purpose
official_measurement_examples.fact: NPPF states the fundamental aim of Green Belt policy is to prevent urban sprawl by keeping land permanently open and identifies five Green Belt purposes.

official_measurement_examples.name: Grey belt definition
official_measurement_examples.fact: The current NPPF defines grey belt as Green Belt land comprising previously developed land and/or other land that does not strongly contribute to specified Green Belt purposes, subject to exclusions for other strongly restrictive policies.

official_measurement_examples.name: Grey belt not automatic approval
official_measurement_examples.fact: Green Belt planning guidance states identifying grey belt does not automatically mean land should be allocated, released or approved; the full relevant NPPF policies still apply.

official_measurement_examples.name: Paragraph 155 conditions
official_measurement_examples.fact: NPPF paragraph 155 treats specified development on grey belt as not inappropriate only where its cumulative policy conditions are met, including remaining-Green-Belt purposes, unmet need, sustainable location and applicable Golden Rules.

official_measurement_examples.name: Green Belt data snapshot limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Data states the Green Belt dataset is an annual-return snapshot and may not reflect boundary changes made after local authorities submitted their returns.

official_measurement_examples.name: Brownfield register distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Data's July 2026 brownfield dataset contains authoritative register entries, while government guidance distinguishes Part 1 register inclusion from Part 2 permission in principle.

official_measurement_examples.name: Permission in principle two stages
official_measurement_examples.fact: Government guidance states permission in principle settles location, land use and amount at the first stage, while technical details consent is still required before development can proceed.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2025-26 statistics timing
official_measurement_examples.fact: MHCLG announced 2025-26 Green Belt statistics on 23 June 2026 with a provisional October-November 2026 release, so the announcement must not be treated as already-published new boundary statistics.

core_rules: Green Belt designation is a planning policy constraint not automatic refusal in every case
grey belt identification is not planning permission
grey belt assessment must retain the current NPPF definition and exclusions
previously developed land is not automatically grey belt approval
Green Belt boundary snapshot data must retain its submission date
Green Belt core classification is not a parcel permission
Part 1 brownfield register inclusion is not permission in principle
Part 2 permission in principle is not technical details consent
permission in principle does not itself authorise development to commence
Golden Rules applicability must be assessed at the relevant proposal and policy stage
very special circumstances must not be presumed from site designation alone
brownfield status does not remove heritage flood contamination or ecological controls
Green Belt data does not determine land ownership access rights or infrastructure capacity
future Green Belt statistics announcement is not the released dataset
no parcel Green Belt or grey-belt clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official MHCLG/GOV.UK and Planning Data sources were checked on 2026-07-26. Current grey-belt policy, July 2026 data snapshots and the June 2026 future statistics announcement were kept distinct; no parcel approval was promoted.
